data_section_full_text:
3.1. Data

Our sample is drawn from countries with sufficient firm-level accounting and returns
data on Global Vantage over the period 1992–2001 to estimate our models. Our sample
selection procedures follow the guidelines established in Ball et al. (2003) (hereafter BRW).
We gather accounting income and dividends data from the Global Vantage Industrial/
Commercial (IC) files. Stock price data is gathered from the Global Vantage Issues file.
Consistent with Ball et al. (2000) (hereafter BKR) and BRW, accounting earnings (NI) is
defined as net income before extraordinary items (IC data 32), and dividends (DIV) is
defined as dividends paid (IC data 36). Change in accounting income (DNIt) is defined
as NIt–NIt–1. All accounting variables are scaled by beginning market value of equity,
defined as price times number of shares outstanding, adjusted for stock splits and
dividends using the Global Vantage adjustment factor. Stock return (RET) is the holding
period return, including dividends, over the firm’s fiscal year. Finally, BKR and BRW
assign a country based on the accounting standards used by the firm to prepare its financial
statements. Since our goal is to examine the impact of country-level institutions on the
properties of reported accounting earnings (regardless of the accounting standard used),
we assigned firm-year observations to countries based on the ISO country code of
incorporation. <sup>15</sup>

Following BRW, we exclude the two extreme percentiles of each variable (NI, DNI and
RET). Second, we exclude each firm-year with a missing value for any of these variables.
Third, we exclude all countries with less than 100 firm-year observations over the ten years.
Finally, we exclude China and Poland because these two countries have socialist legal
origin, and exclude Bermuda and the Cayman Islands because we lack institutional
variables for these two countries. <sup>16</sup> These restrictions result in a final sample of 86,927
